A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RPF/RSF retrosynthesis framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and matchable; v2 also includes a paper checklist. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original USPTO-50k experiments measuring exact-match accuracy, round-trip performance, and sampling and steering ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds inference-time comparisons and forward-synthesis model error measurements in Appendices B.3 and C.

M1.justification: The discrete-flow objectives, graph transformer, synthon conditioning, and FK/SMC steering procedure are unchanged. Product-context inputs and the Appendix D Runge–Kutta sampler already appear in v1; the Table 3 label swap does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: USPTO-50k remains the only dataset, with the same single-step retrosynthesis and forward-synthesis round-trip setting. The added timing and forward-model diagnostics examine existing data and components without introducing a new chemical domain or reaction scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds the Chimera ensemble to the exact-match comparison in Table 1. Its new runtime comparison also includes GLN, LocalRetro, and RetroBridge, which previously appeared in accuracy comparisons. Existing comparator rows are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a timing evaluation across K = 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 particles for sampling 100 reactants on an RTX 3090. Appendix C adds direct top-k evaluation of Molecular Transformer. These extend the evaluation design; the original splits, preprocessing, training budget, and principal sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds particle-count runtime scaling and expands the forward-model error analysis with direct accuracy and mis-scoring measurements. Table 3 reverses the result attribution for the product-context ablation. The existing synthon-allocation, sampling-step, steering-control, and Runge–Kutta analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The uncertainty values in Table 1 and the 5.46 ± 2.95-second timing report are retained. The new checklist explains that ablation error bars are omitted because of computational cost, but adds no run counts, seeds, uncertainty definitions, intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Headline RPF/RSF scores remain unchanged. Table 1 adds Chimera scores of 59.6/82.8/89.2/94.2, leading at k = 3, 5, 10. Table 3 swaps condition labels, assigning 67.7 rather than 59.7 top-1 accuracy to RSF with product context; no rerun is established. New results include particle-dependent runtimes, Molecular Transformer accuracy of 75/82/83/83, and reported mis-scoring rates of 25% without steering versus 14% with steering.

T1.justification: The discrete-flow and FK formulations, training loss, graph-feature formulas, and Appendix D sampling equations are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The introduction recharacterizes the proposed family from two template-free models to template-free/semi-template models, and contribution 3 explicitly includes semi-template methods in its superiority claim. The central novelty claim and the headline 60% top-1 and 19% round-trip improvement claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 qualifies the approximately 20% advantage as applying to methods without ensembling and discusses complementarity with Chimera. Appendix B.3 newly argues that roughly 30-second sampling is practical for multistep planning, without evaluating multistep planning. Appendix C expands attention to errors in the forward-model feasibility proxy.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies 3.38 million model parameters and documents the hardware and output budget for the timing comparison. The listed code repository changes from DSL-Lab/retroflow to DSL-Lab/RetroSynFlow. Existing architecture, optimizer, training, and preprocessing details are retained; actual repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds four cited works: Chimera, Laabid et al.'s graph-diffusion work, and Coley and Segler papers concerning synthesis planning. It acknowledges earlier forward-model use in multistep planning, distinguishes semi-template approaches, and positions RSF as complementary to Chimera. The broader related-work structure remains intact.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the introduction, comparison discussion, and related work. v2 adds a supplementary contents page, divides Appendix B into named subsections, appends the NeurIPS checklist, and updates the publication footer. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds timing and forward-model accuracy tables, numbered 6 and 8, and a Chimera row and explanatory footnote in Table 1. All twelve existing figures are retained with layout shifts. Earlier Tables 6 and 7 become Tables 7 and 9, and the supplement gains contents and checklist layouts.

improvement.justification: The Chimera comparison and new runtime and forward-model diagnostics make v2 more informative about competitive performance, computational cost, and reward reliability. These are useful but limited gains over v1. The Table 3 label reversal remains unexplained, the new chemical-validity mis-scoring measurements lack procedural detail, and the abstract retains its broad 20% advantage wording despite the closer Chimera comparison.
